newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. envoy to meet Iraqi Kurd leader next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to meet Iraqi Kurd leader next week.

text.p: The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) said on Friday its leader would meet a senior U.S. diplomat next week for talks on ending figting between the KDP and a rival Kurdish group in northern Iraq.

A Turkish foreign ministry official said the meeting between KDP head Massoud Barzani and U.S. assistant secretary state Robert Pelletreau was likely to be in Turkey and would probably be held on on Sunday or Monday, later than had been previously thought.
Barzani on Thursday raised the stakes of the U.S. peace bid in northern Iraq by threatening to call for Baghdad's help in his struggle with the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
The KDP got help from Iraqi forces six weeks ago to take the main regional city of Arbil. The Kurdish group then pushed the PUK out of its other stronghold Sulaimaniya.
Washington says Pelletreau also plans to meet PUK chief Jalal Talabani.
Barzani's fighters on Friday advanced to within two km (one mile) of the town of Koy Sanjak, held by the PUK, in a bid to relieve a partial seige of Arbil.
